generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table, never NULL; generated rows are appended after the compact rows so PKs never collide with compact PKs.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from the parent table's PK pool restricted to PKs actually present in the written instance (compact + generated); 5% NULL only when the column is nullable; never plant NULL on a NOT NULL FK.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity: Uniform integer in [1, 6]; never negative. Per-column exceptions override this rule.
generic_sampling_rules.char_enum: Pick uniformly from the enum list defined in per_column_exceptions; canonical values only, no case/whitespace variants.
generic_sampling_rules.char_code: Pick from a small fixed pool of 3-6 short strings; 10% near-variants (case/whitespace).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Pick from a pool of 20 first/last names; 20-40% duplicate share across rows.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_address: Synthesize 'NNN Street Name\nCity, ST ZIP'; 20-40% duplicate share.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Uniform timestamp in [2015-01-01, 2018-12-31] formatted '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; 20-40% duplicate share.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numeric: For each listed literal L, include L-1, L, L+1 within the column's declared domain.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_text: For each listed literal L, include L and a case-variant (lower/upper).
generic_sampling_rules.tie_order: Ensure at least 3 rows share the tie value at the listed rank; ranks must be reachable at the table size.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: 5% NULL on nullable columns; at least one NULL row per nullable column; NULLs are planted after all value-shaping rules and are never overwritten.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_share: For DISTINCT targets, copy a non-NULL source value into 20-50% of rows; skip NULL cells.

apt_type_code ties_for_order_limit on AVG(room_count)/SUM(bathroom_count) at ranks 1 and 3 are not guaranteed by the tie rule alone; the tie rule only forces shared apt_type_code values, and aggregate ties are left to natural variation.
The instance must be a copy of the compact database plus appended rows; the writer must receive the original database path and FK pools must be restricted to PKs present in the written instance.
